about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Odia bytes (fonts SHREE-ORI7-0600..0604 = S06xx892.TTF and WORI7001/2.TTF; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-ORI-0600..0604 = S06xx0F2.TTF draw the same bytes, except ₹ 3C which only WORI7001/2 have), answered by Shree's own composers S8OriU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Ori764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes) for the same keystroke. bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code (bytes 80-9F are raw bytes: in a document they sit on their Windows-1252 code points, except 8F and 90 which the fonts map at U+008F/U+0090). Every probe set and every vendor keyboard was captured twice in separate processes: identical (the only difference is the random unit count the 7 composer returns for "no answer"). kind: vendor-key = a key (layer 0, Ctrl+Space, or the composer raw code layer) of one of the 8 shipped .ORI keyboards loaded from its ORIGINAL path (the composers switch typing mode by name: ENG/PHONETIC answer a consonant with its virama form, NEWROMA/ROMA are phonetic, INSCRIPT types E7/E8/E9 as େ + length mark); source names the keyboard, key and codes. canonical = probe in Shree's typing order for Odia: the e-sign େ (code 6C) struck FIRST, ୋ = େ + C + ା, ୌ = େ + C + ୗ, ୈ = େ + C + ୖ, every other sign after the cluster, ଂ ଁ ଃ after the sign, the reph (code 40) struck AFTER the letter (and its signs), ra-phala = code D1 (F7), ya-phala = code D2 (BF, the Unicode composer writes ୍ୟ = 0B4D 0B5F), conjuncts through the link code 64 (the 7 composer writes the conjunct glyph or the subjoined form); canonical:pending-link = a word-final virama (visible FA); canonical:halant / canonical:half = codes 44 / D5 (Unicode virama + ZWNJ / ZWJ: visible FA, no conjunct); canonical:ୱ = ଓ + link + ବ (48 B4). preferred: vendor key, then the reph struck before ଂ ଁ ଃ (sign, reph, tail: the reph F6 sits on the letter; struck after the tail it sits over the ଂ - both accepted), then for ର୍ର the reph reading (C0 FF F6) over the ra-phala one (C0 FF F7), then canonical, then fewer bytes (ଧ୍ୟ: link + ୟ = the ligature 9A, the ya-phala key D2 = 99 BF; କ୍ଷ: the code 5C = E4, C + link + ଷ = 4C FF FA CC; both accepted), then more probes; accepted keeps every canonical spelling. alt:* = the composer answer for another typing order or a visibly different form (reph struck first or before the post sign, େ struck after the letter, a sign before the phala code, ର + link + C = ର with C subjoined instead of the reph, C + link + ଯ = visible halant + ଯ instead of the ya-phala) - kept, not used as truth. quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the codes mean (it keeps only the first of two ଂ ଁ ଃ, drops a reph or ୃ or link after the ra-phala, drops the reph after ୃ, puts a nukta after େ), or the 7 composer dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (the nukta, ୱ ଵ ୡ ଓଁ ୄ ୢ ୣ, E7/E8/E9, ॥ × ÷ — – “ ” etc.: nothing; a reph struck after ି + ଂ), or a code only the 7 composer types (E1 ba-phala FD, E0 -> E3, 51 -> 23), or a carrier byte 07 - kept for evidence, not used. Unicode keys are what the Unicode composer wrote (ଡ଼ ଢ଼ come back precomposed U+0B5C U+0B5D, which NFC decomposes - a table needs both forms; ଅ + ା is filed under ଆ). Rules with examples: ori7-patterns.txt.

fontCheck.method: fonts/family-check.json (fontcmp.js): (3,1) cmap of the 7 faces WORI7001.TTF (name SHREE-ORI7-0603), WORI7002.TTF (SHREE-ORI7-0604), S0600892..S0604892.TTF (SHREE-ORI7-0600..0604) and the 4/5/6 faces S06000F2..S06040F2.TTF (SHREE-ORI-0600..0604); per code glyph id, advance, sha1 of the glyf bytes; same-design pairs compared outline by outline; every code drawn by glyph index (fonts/codes-*.png, fonts/wori7001-all.png, fonts/diff-wori-vs-456.png).
fontCheck.result: S06xx892 (SHREE-ORI7-06xx) and S06xx0F2 (SHREE-ORI-06xx) are identical code by code: 216 codes, same glyph ids, same outline bytes and advances (0600, 0601, 0602, 0603, 0604: 216/216 each). WORI7001/WORI7002 carry the same family names as S0603892/S0604892 (SHREE-ORI7-0603/0604) and add ₹ at 3C (217 codes, glyph ids shifted by one); against S06030F2 7 codes have touched-up outlines (62 67 97 A1 A3 BE C7) and against S06040F2 5 (82 88 89 C6 F4) - the same characters, same advances (rendered side by side). Bytes 80 81 8D 8E 9D 9E have no glyph in any face; 8F and 90 sit on U+008F/U+0090 (the C1 code points), every other byte 80-9F on its Windows-1252 code point. ONE table serves both families; only ₹ (3C) is missing from every 4/5/6 face and from S06xx892.

counts.notProbed: A conjunct slot holds at most 4 codes, so these are not in the truth: C୍C + ୈ/ୋ/ୌ (େ + C + link + C + length mark = 5 codes), C୍C + reph + a sign, C୍C + sign + tail, three-consonant clusters other than C୍C + ୍ର / ୍ୟ (5 codes: C link C link C), C୍C୍ର / C୍C୍ୟ + a sign. ୱ after a virama (C୍ୱ, U+0B71) and ଵ (U+0B35), ୡ, ଓଁ, ୄ ୢ ୣ, ॥, × ÷, — – “ ”, + ; = [ ] and the Vedic marks have no 7 spelling at all: the 7 composer types nothing for their codes. The Unicode ya-phala ୍ଯ (U+0B2F) has no canonical spelling: the composer writes C + link + ଯ as visible halant + full ଯ (FA BE, kept as alt); Shree's own ya-phala is ୍ୟ (U+0B5F) = BF.
